body_edits.before: [^v1-i1-transparency]: Neil W. Ashcroft and N. David Mermin, *Solid State Physics* (1976), ch. 8 and 12, on Bloch electrons: in a perfectly periodic potential the stationary states carry current without degradation, and resistance arises from deviations from periodicity (lattice vibrations, impurities, defects). The diamond-cubic silicon lattice has a two-atom basis and a lattice constant of 0.543 nm, about $5 \times 10^{22}$ atoms per cubic centimeter.
body_edits.after: [^v1-i1-transparency]: For Bloch states and the resulting dispersion, see Nicola Marzari, MIT 3.23, [lecture 9](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/3-23-electrical-optical-and-magnetic-properties-of-materials-fall-2007/49728ee6fbac8503c94b5a9aab74242c_lec9.pdf) (2007). The static periodic potential does not cause random resistive collisions in this independent-electron picture; it still determines bands, effective masses and diffraction. ‘Invisible’ is that limited analogy, not a claim that a lattice cannot be detected or that interacting, finite crystals must have zero resistance. Silicon’s two-atom primitive cell differs from its conventional cubic cell: the latter has eight atoms, a side of 0.543 nm and hence about $5 \times 10^{22}$ atoms per cubic centimeter; see del Alamo, [lecture 2](https://web.mit.edu/6.012/www/SP07-L2.pdf), p. 3.
body_edits.reason: Replace the from-memory textbook citation with inspected teaching sources; retain the metaphor while distinguishing ballistic Bloch propagation from literal vacuum.

body_edits.before: [^v1-i1-dirac]: P. A. M. Dirac, “A Theory of Electrons and Protons,” *Proceedings of the Royal Society A* 126 (1930): 360–365. The correspondence between a semiconductor’s filled valence band and Dirac’s sea is an analogy with a shared mathematics, not an identity; modern quantum field theory no longer describes the vacuum as a filled sea. Silicon’s band gap is about 1.12 eV at room temperature and its intrinsic carrier density about $10^{10}$ per cubic centimeter; see S. M. Sze and Kwok K. Ng, *Physics of Semiconductor Devices*, 3rd ed. (2007).
body_edits.after: [^v1-i1-dirac]: P. A. M. Dirac, [‘A Theory of Electrons and Protons’](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1930.0013), *Proceedings of the Royal Society A* 126 (1930): 360–365, and [‘Quantised Singularities in the Electromagnetic Field’](https://doi.org/10.1098/rspa.1931.0130), 133 (1931): 60–72. The latter replaces the proton identification with an anti-electron. A semiconductor hole is an effective excitation, not a positron; ‘cancel’ means recombination, not literal matter–antimatter annihilation. Efficient LEDs generally use direct-gap materials, unlike silicon. For silicon’s 1.12 eV gap and intrinsic carrier density near $10^{10}$ cm$^{-3}$ at 300 K, see C. A. Ross, MIT 3.15, [‘Carrier Fundamentals’](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/3-15-electrical-optical-magnetic-materials-and-devices-fall-2006/a3b94baf512eac5e3272b6f2f9b59467_lecture1.pdf), pp. 1–2. More fully, $n_i=\sqrt{N_cN_v}\,e^{-E_g/(2k_BT)}$, where $N_c,N_v$ are effective densities of states; the omitted prefactor itself varies with temperature. The exponential alone is not the fraction of atoms supplying carriers.
body_edits.reason: Verify Dirac’s two stages and define the semiconductor analogy and intrinsic-carrier prefactor without turning the main passage into a technical qualification.

body_edits.before: [^v1-i1-donor]: W. Kohn and J. M. Luttinger, “Theory of Donor States in Silicon,” *Physical Review* 98 (1955): 915–922. Silicon’s relative permittivity is about 11.7; the simple hydrogen-like estimate gives a binding energy of a few hundredths of an electron-volt and a radius of two to three nanometers, and the measured ionization energy of phosphorus in silicon is about 0.045 eV. Purity figures for electronic-grade silicon are commonly quoted as nine to eleven “nines.” A doping level of one part per million is about $5 \times 10^{16}$ atoms per cubic centimeter, against an intrinsic carrier density near $10^{10}$.
body_edits.after: [^v1-i1-donor]: W. Kohn and J. M. Luttinger, [‘Theory of Donor States in Silicon’](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRev.98.915), *Physical Review* 98 (1955): 915–922. The hydrogen picture uses screened interaction and effective mass, not changed fundamental constants. An isotropic estimate with relative permittivity about 11.7 and mass about $0.26m_e$ gives a radius near 2.4 nm and binding near 0.026 eV; valley anisotropy and the donor’s immediate surroundings matter for the actual ground state. Phosphorus’s measured binding is about 0.045 eV; see Ross, [‘Carrier Fundamentals’](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/3-15-electrical-optical-magnetic-materials-and-devices-fall-2006/a3b94baf512eac5e3272b6f2f9b59467_lecture1.pdf), p. 1. At room temperature, dilute donors can be largely ionized even though this exceeds $k_BT$; state populations, not a hard energy cutoff, determine ionization. One-part-per-million doping gives about $5 \times 10^{16}$ donors per cm$^3$. For the purity scale, Tokuyama specifies [eleven-nines polysilicon](https://www.tokuyama.co.jp/eng/products/electronic_materials/polysilicon.html/); purity specifications depend on the impurities counted.
body_edits.reason: Verify the donor model, distinguish the simple estimate from measured phosphorus binding, and link a producer’s purity specification.

body_edits.before: [^v1-i1-czochralski]: J. Czochralski, “Ein neues Verfahren zur Messung der Kristallisationsgeschwindigkeit der Metalle,” *Zeitschrift für physikalische Chemie* 92 (1918): 219–221. The pen-and-tin story is traditional and may be embellished. Modern 300 mm silicon ingots run to roughly two meters and well over a hundred kilograms.
body_edits.after: [^v1-i1-czochralski]: J. Czochralski, [‘Ein neues Verfahren zur Messung der Kristallisationsgeschwindigkeit der Metalle’](https://doi.org/10.1515/zpch-1918-9212), *Zeitschrift für physikalische Chemie* 92 (1918): 219–221. The work dates to 1916; the pen-and-tin story is traditional and may be embellished. See [‘Jan Czochralski and His Method of Pulling Crystals’](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/E735C7FCE5CFC8F1A8E9799CE07046E1/S0883769400015463a.pdf/jan-czochralski-and-his-method-of-pulling-crystals.pdf), *MRS Bulletin* (2004). Intel’s [*From Sand to Silicon*](https://download.intel.com/newsroom/kits/chipmaking/pdfs/Sand-to-Silicon_45nm-Version.pdf) (2009), ‘Monocrystalline Silicon Ingot,’ illustrates the hundred-kilogram scale; ingot dimensions and mass vary with the growth process.
body_edits.reason: Link the original paper and history; keep the anecdote explicitly traditional and use a sourced industrial scale rather than an uncited precise modern size.

body_edits.before: [^v1-i1-switchenergy]: Rolf Landauer, "Irreversibility and Heat Generation in the Computing Process," *IBM Journal of Research and Development* 5 (1961): 183–191, for the erasure bound; for dynamic switching energy in CMOS, see Neil H. E. Weste and David Money Harris, *CMOS VLSI Design: A Circuits and Systems Perspective*, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley, 2011), ch. 5. The femtojoule figure is an order-of-magnitude illustration for a logic gate with its local wiring; it varies widely with technology and load. (AI-added, from memory; to be verified.)
body_edits.after: [^v1-i1-switchenergy]: Neil H. E. Weste and David Money Harris, *CMOS VLSI Design: A Circuits and Systems Perspective*, 4th ed. (Addison-Wesley, 2011), ch. 5; Harris’s accompanying [‘Power’ lecture](https://pages.hmc.edu/harris/cmosvlsi/4e/lect/lect7.pdf), pp. 5–8, derives $CV^2$ for a full charge–discharge cycle. The femtofarad/volt example is illustrative, not a specification for every gate. For the erasure bound, see Landauer (1961) and Bennett (2003), cited below: an ideal isothermal reset of one initially unknown, equally probable bit gives $k_BT\ln 2$. Switching a load and erasing information are distinct operations; their energy scales are compared here, not equated.
body_edits.reason: Verify textbook edition and author lecture; replace the unverified tag with scoped evidence and distinguish the two energy costs.

body_edits.before: [^v1-i1-darwinism]: Wojciech H. Zurek, “Quantum Darwinism,” *Nature Physics* 5 (2009): 181–188. (AI draft 2026-11-12; unverified.) Quantum Darwinism is a research program with experimental support in small systems; the link to “informational gravity” and to Chapter 1's recipe census is the author's conjecture.
body_edits.after: [^v1-i1-darwinism]: Wojciech H. Zurek, [‘Quantum Darwinism’](https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys1202), *Nature Physics* 5 (2009): 181–188. For an experimental test of redundant records in a small spin environment, see T. K. Unden et al., [‘Revealing the Emergence of Classicality Using Nitrogen-Vacancy Centers’](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.123.140402), *Physical Review Letters* 123 (2019): 140402. The copied information concerns selected pointer states; arbitrary unknown quantum states cannot be freely cloned. The link to informational gravity remains the author’s conjecture. A short description of repeated structure is not by itself a probability measure over worlds or a physical mechanism of replication.
body_edits.reason: Verify theory and experimental foothold; preserve the conjecture and explain which kind of copying the evidence supports.

body_edits.before: [^v1-i1-diode]: In the ideal diffusion model, $I=I_S\left(e^{qV/(k_BT)}-1\right)$: current $I$, reverse saturation current $I_S$, junction voltage $V$, elementary charge $q$, absolute temperature $T$ and Boltzmann constant $k_B$. See del Alamo, MIT 6.012, [lecture 14](https://web.mit.edu/6.012/www/SP07-L14.pdf) (2007), pp. 13–16. This is a model with a range of validity, not an exact law for every diode; recombination, series resistance, high injection and breakdown require further treatment.
body_edits.after: [^v1-i1-diode]: In the ideal diffusion model, $I=I_S\left(e^{qV/(k_BT)}-1\right)$: current $I$, reverse saturation current $I_S$, junction voltage $V$, elementary charge $q$, absolute temperature $T$ and Boltzmann constant $k_B$. See del Alamo, MIT 6.012, [lecture 14](https://web.mit.edu/6.012/www/SP07-L14.pdf) (2007), pp. 13–16. This is a model with a range of validity, not an exact law for every diode; recombination, series resistance, high injection and breakdown require further treatment. The tenfold increase per roughly 60 mV is the forward-current approximation at 300 K with ideality factor one; the depleted layer in the figure uses the approximation that mobile charge there is negligible.
